intro.title: useOnlineStatus
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom Vue composable called `useOnlineStatus` that detects whether the user's device is online or offline. You will learn how to use the browser's `navigator.onLine` property and event listeners to track network connectivity changes in real-time. The main technologies involved are Vue's Composition API and JavaScript's `window` events. By the end, you'll have a reusable composable that can be integrated into any Vue component to display the current online status.
intro.usecase: The useOnlineStatus hook is essential for building resilient applications that need to adapt to changing network conditions. In real-world products like collaborative document editors (Google Docs, Notion) or messaging apps (Slack, WhatsApp), this pattern displays connection status indicators and gracefully handles offline scenarios. Developers implement it in dashboards to show real-time data availability, in e-commerce carts to prevent order submission failures, and in progressive web apps to enable offline functionality. This ensures users always know their connection state and prevents frustrating experiences when network connectivity changes unexpectedly.
